rot.openFile.ideia.colunas.e1: Attack: a file with no pawn of either side is an open file. Here it is the d-file: the rook on d1 can travel up it into Black's camp.
rot.openFile.ideia.colunas.e2: On the c-file there is only the black pawn on c6. With no white pawn on it, it is a half-open file for White: the rook on c1 presses that pawn.
rot.openFile.ideia.colunas.e3: In the same way, the e-file, where there is only the white pawn on e4, is half-open for Black.
rot.openFile.ideia.colunas.l1: The rook goes up the open file to d7. The seventh rank is the second rank of Black's camp, where the pawns that have not advanced stand: the rook attacks b7 and f7.
rot.openFile.ideia.colunas.l2: Black defends the b7-pawn with the rook. The one on f7 is already defended by the rook on f8 and by the king.
rot.openFile.ideia.colunas.l3: The other rook comes to the d-file, behind the first one: the rooks are doubled. The one on d1 supports the one on d7 and keeps the file for White.
rot.openFile.ideia.colunas.l4: In positions like this one, the rook is usually worth more on the open file, because it leads to the seventh rank.
rot.openFile.ideia.colunas.l5: But if Black moved first, the rook on f8 would go to d8, contest the file and trade the rooks. With no free square to break in through, the open file stops paying off.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.e1: Attack: this position comes from a Slav Defence, Exchange Variation, played on Lichess. The trades in the centre left the d-file open, and the rook on d1 is already on it.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.e2: Black has not yet put a rook on the d-file. Look at their seventh rank: both bishops are there, and neither is defended.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.p: Find the move that uses the open d-file.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.certo: The rook goes up the open file to the seventh rank and attacks both bishops at once: a double attack.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.revela: The rook goes to d7, along the open file, and attacks both bishops on the seventh rank: a double attack.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.err.c1e3.1: With this move, Black brings the f8-rook to d8, contests the file and trades the rooks.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.err.c1e3.2: Back to the position: the d-file still belongs to White alone. Use it before Black contests it.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.err.g2f1.1: With this move, Black brings the b7-bishop to d5 and closes the d-file to the rook on d1.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.err.g2f1.2: Back to the position: look for a move of the d1-rook along the open file.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.err.d1d6.1: With this move, the bishop on e7 captures the rook, and the e5-pawn only wins back the bishop: White gives a rook for a bishop.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.err.d1d6.2: Back to the position: take the rook further, to the bishops' rank.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.fora: That move does not use the d-file. Look for a move of the rook on d1.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.volta: Try again: use the open d-file.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.l0: Black cannot save both bishops with a single move.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.l1: The a8-rook goes to d8: it attacks the rook on d7 and starts to contest the file.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.l2: The rook captures the bishop on b7 and gets out of the attack. White has won a piece.
rot.openFile.ideia.eslava.l3: The open file took the rook to the seventh rank, where Black's undefended pieces stood. Taking the file before the opponent often pays off like this.
rot.openFile.demos.regra.1: Attacking demonstration: now let us think from Black's side, in a game from Lichess. The d-file is open. The white knight on d6 is attacked by the bishop on e5 and defended only by the rook on d1.
rot.openFile.demos.regra.2: The rook goes to the open file. Now the knight has two attackers and one defender, and it cannot leave: if it does, the rook on d7 captures the one on d1.
rot.openFile.demos.regra.3: White has no way to save the knight and advances the h3-pawn, to make room for the king.
rot.openFile.demos.regra.5: The d1-rook captures the rook on d6.
rot.openFile.demos.regra.6: The bishop recaptures. Black has won the knight: the rook on the open file added an attacker against it.
rot.openFile.demos.regra2.1: Attacking demonstration: another game from Lichess. White has no d-pawn, and the black pawn is on d6: for White, the d-file is half-open. The rook on d3 is on it.
rot.openFile.demos.regra2.2: The black knight on d4 occupies an outpost, supported by the e5-pawn. Notice also that the queens on d5 and e6 attack each other.
rot.openFile.demos.regra2.3: The rook captures the knight on d4. If the e5-pawn recaptures, the queen on d5 captures the queen on e6.
rot.openFile.demos.regra2.4: Black captures the queen on d5, so as not to lose their own.
rot.openFile.demos.regra2.5: The rook recaptures on d5. White has won the knight.
rot.openFile.demos.regra2.6: On the half-open file, the rook pressed whatever Black had on it. Here it was the outpost knight, and it fell.
rot.openFile.demos.excecao.1: Defensive demonstration: now let us think from Black's side. White has doubled the rooks on the open e-file, and the rook on e6 attacks the queen on f6.
rot.openFile.demos.excecao.2: With both rooks on the e-file, the f2-pawn is defended only by the king. The queen on f6 and the bishop on d4 attack it.
rot.openFile.demos.excecao.3: The queen captures the f2-pawn with check, defended by the bishop on d4.
rot.openFile.demos.excecao.4: The king only has h1 to get out of check.
rot.openFile.demos.excecao.5: The queen gives mate on f3: it covers g2, and the bishop on d4 covers g1.
rot.openFile.demos.excecao.6: White controlled the open file, but left the king without defence. Before doubling the rooks, check what the opponent is threatening.
rot.openFile.pratica.valeAqui.enunciado: Your rook on d7, on the seventh rank, attacks the queen on b7. Is it worth taking it right away? Play as White and find the best move.
rot.openFile.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The knight on e5 was attacking your queen. It stepped away with check on b4, and only then did the rook capture the queen on b7. Before capturing, check what the opponent is threatening.
rot.openFile.pratica.valeAqui.err.d7b7: The rook captures the queen, but the knight on e5 captures your queen on g4, and Black wins the material back. Look for a check first.
rot.openFile.pratica.valeAqui.err.g4g8: The queen gives check on g8, but the king captures it. Look for another check.
rot.openFile.pratica.valeAqui.err.g4g7: The queen gives check on g7, but the king captures it. Look for another check.
rot.openFile.pratica.valeAqui.err.f1d1: The rook on f1 supports the one on d7, but the black queen captures the rook on d7, and the knight on e5 also covers d7. Look for a check.
rot.openFile.pratica.aberta.enunciado: The e-file is open, and your rook on e7 has reached the seventh rank, but the rook on e8 attacks it. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.openFile.pratica.aberta.fim: The e1-rook captured the bishop on e6 and was doubled with the one on e7, which now had a defender. The black rook captured on e7, and yours recaptured: White has won the bishop.
rot.openFile.pratica.aberta.err.e7e8: The rook captures on e8 with check, but the a8-rook recaptures, and the bishop on e6 stays in play. Look for a move that doubles the rooks.
rot.openFile.pratica.aberta.err.e7c7: The rook leaves the e-file, and the e8-rook takes control of it. Look for a move that doubles the rooks.
rot.openFile.pratica.aberta.err.c1e3: The bishop attacks the queen, but it captures the b2-pawn, and your rook on e7 is still attacked. Look for a move that doubles the rooks.
rot.openFile.pratica.semiPreto.enunciado: Now let us think from Black's side. You have no d-pawn: for you, the d-file is half-open. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.openFile.pratica.semiPreto.fim: The rook captured the d5-pawn and attacked the queen on d4. The queen captured the rook, and the bishop captured the queen: Black has won the queen for a rook.
rot.openFile.pratica.semiPreto.err.d7c8: The queen leaves the d-file, and the rook on d6 loses its support. Look for a capture on the d-file.
rot.openFile.pratica.semiPreto.err.d7c7: The queen leaves the d-file, and the rook on d6 loses its support. Look for a capture on the d-file.
rot.openFile.pratica.semiPreto.err.g8h7: The king goes to h7, but threatens nothing, and White gains time to defend the d5-pawn. Look for a capture on the d-file.
